title: Hotpatch runbook, severity matrix, and backport policy for LTS & rolling channels
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Create a pragmatic, auditable runbook and policy for performing hotpatches across Redwood's release channels (hosted rolling, dedicated, and LTS). This ticket codifies: severity criteria, how and when to open a patch branch, the backport policy for LTS and maintenance branches, rollout gates for safe deployment, and required tooling/automation changes to minimize human error. This is intended to replace ad-hoc procedures observed during recent incidents and to align expectations with Product, Support, and SRE teams.
severity_matrix:
S0 (Sev0) - Production outage affecting >30% of customer traffic OR data corruption: immediate paged response, launch hotpatch branch from main->patch, emergency approval required, automatic global rollback plan, target MTTR < 30 minutes.
S1 (Sev1) - Severe degradation for high-value customers or critical feature regressions: page on-call, create patch branch, prioritize rapid backport to currently supported LTS versions where applicable, target MTTR < 2 hours.
S2 (Sev2) - Functional bug with workarounds, minor performance regressions: triage in normal business hours, schedule patch in next maintenance window; backport if reproducible in LTS with customer impact.
S3 - Minor/non-blocking issues and cosmetic bugs: include in next regular release cadence, no hotpatching unless escalated.
runbook_steps:
1) Triage & classification: Support or monitoring team files a ticket and tags severity using the matrix above.
2) Convene incident owner & release lead: designate a patch owner and engineering reviewer.
3) Branching: if hotpatch needed, create patch branch naming convention patch/<release>-<semver>-hotfix-<id> (e.g., patch/2.4.1-hotfix-9467). Branch must be forked from the commit that is currently deployed to affected channel (determine via Deploy Dashboard).
4) Patch dev & CI: minimal diff, focused tests, and a changelog entry. Ensure automated smoke tests for the affected path run and pass.
5) Approval: emergency approval gate requires one release lead + one security reviewer (if security_related=true). Record approvals in PR and incident ticket.
6) Canary rollout: deploy to a canary subset (configurable, default 2% traffic) using rollout gates in Console. Monitor latency, error rate, saturation for 30 minutes (or shorter for Sev0 if risk justifies).
7) Gradual ramp: if canary is healthy, follow ramp schedule (2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with at least one successful monitoring window between steps.
8) Backporting: open backport PRs against LTS branches per policy. For LTS, backport required for S0/S1; for rolling channel, backport optional.
9) Communication: notify customers per SLA, update status page, include CVE/impact if security-related.
10) Postmortem & release: create a blameless postmortem within 7 days and include backport status and ROI analysis.
patch_branch_strategy:
- Naming: patch/<major>.<minor>.<patch>-hotfix-<ticket>. Example: patch/2.4.3-hotfix-9467.
- Source commit: branch off the exact deployed commit SHA for the channel experiencing the issue (use Deploy Dashboard to resolve).
- Scope: changes must be minimal and revertible. Large refactors are not allowed in hotpatch branches.
- Merge policy: two reviewers minimum, one must be a release lead. For security fixes, a security reviewer sign-off string must be present in PR description.
- Tagging: every hotpatch merge creates a semantic-release patch (e.g., 2.4.3) and triggers packaging pipeline to produce artifacts for Dedicated and Private channels.
backport_policy:
- LTS branches: Any S0 or S1 regression must be backported to the active LTS branches supported by customers within 72 hours. For S0 fixes, backport is mandatory and prioritized. For S1, engineering must assess risk vs customer impact; if customers on LTS are affected, backport within 72 hours.
- Rolling (hosted) channel: backport only if the regression would recur in rolling deployments or if it affects core shared services.
- Private deployments: produce vendor-friendly patch artifacts (release notes and upgrade scripts).
- Automated cherry-pick tooling: add metadata to the incident ticket to automate creation of initial backport PRs (see links).
- Version labeling: backport PR titles must include the original hotpatch ticket key and target branch (e.g., "Backport ENG-9467 to runtime-2.3-lts").
gating_rules:
- Tests: Must pass full regression suite for the module + smoke suite defined for hotpatches.
- Metrics: Error Rate <= baseline + 3x statistical noise, Latency P95 within 15% of baseline. Any breach halts rollout.
- Approvals: emergency deploy requires release lead + one peer reviewer + security if flagged.
- Canary duration: 30 minutes standard; can be shortened to 10 minutes for S0 with explicit release lead signoff.
- Auto-rollback hook: if critical metric breaches during any stage, rollback automatically to previous deployment artifact and create a rollback ticket referencing the hotpatch PR.
upgrade_tooling_changes:
- CI: Add a 'hotpatch' pipeline that runs a focused smoke test matrix and a backport generation job.
- Deploy Console: Introduce a 'hotpatch mode' that enforces smaller canaries and requires explicit approval gates.
- Cherry-pick helper: small bot that creates draft backport PRs to target branches and labels them with 'hotpatch-backport'.
- Release notes automation: auto-populate hotpatch entry and affected versions into the release-notes dashboard for customer communication.
testing_and_validation:
- Local repro guidance included in PR template.
- Mandatory smoke tests: authentication flows, inference latency on a small prompt set, KV cache integrity tests.
- Canary health dashboard snapshot must be attached to the incident ticket.
- If tests cannot be automated within 24 hours, the release lead must document manual test plan and sign off.
monitoring_and_postmortem:
- Monitoring hooks: create temporary Grafana dashboard with dashboard id logged in ticket and configure alerts to escalate on threshold breaches.
- Postmortem timeline: incident declared -> 72-hour preliminary findings -> full blameless postmortem within 7 days.
- Required artifacts for postmortem: PR diff, canary metrics, rollback logs, customer list impacted, and timeline of decisions.
- Follow-ups: create tickets for any tooling gaps or repeat failure modes discovered.

notes: This document is intentionally prescriptive for high-severity incidents but intentionally permissive for S2/S3 to avoid over-burdening the release process. We will iterate on thresholds after two hotpatch cycles and one postmortem review. Ensure desk procedures for support are updated in the customer communication playbook.
